claims.text: Starting the container plus migrating takes seconds (create to destroy about 9 s in a run); a repository test on a ready database takes tens of milliseconds (second test 32-64 ms), the class's first test up to about a second (726 ms-1 s).
claims.source_hint: verified by execution on git archive stage-2: docker events timestamps and dotnet test verbosity=normal (scratchpad it-a/evidence-tc.txt)

claims.text: xUnit creates a new instance of the test class for every test method it runs, so the constructor runs once per test.
claims.source_hint: xunit.net docs: Shared Context between Tests (constructor and Dispose)

claims.text: A test class that declares IClassFixture<T> gets one T created by xUnit for all its tests; xUnit passes that same instance to the constructor of every test class instance (here the primary-constructor parameter `database`).
claims.source_hint: xunit.net docs: Shared Context between Tests, Class Fixtures; EfOrderRepositoryTests.cs:14-15

claims.text: When a class fixture implements IAsyncLifetime, xUnit awaits its InitializeAsync before the class's first test and its DisposeAsync after the class's last test.
claims.source_hint: xunit.net docs: Shared Context (IAsyncLifetime); PostgresFixture.cs:21-33 comment

claims.text: A class fixture is per declaring test class: at stage-2 OrdersApiTests declares IClassFixture<ApiFactory>, and ApiFactory holds its own PostgresFixture (property Database), so a full run of DonHang.Tests creates two postgres:17.6-alpine containers.
claims.source_hint: OrdersApiTests.cs:13; ApiFactory.cs:22-29; verified by execution: docker events shows 2 creates for a full run

claims.text: Tests sharing a class fixture share one database, so rows saved by one test are still there for the next unless something empties the tables first.
claims.source_hint: PostgresFixture.cs (one container per fixture); outline item 5

claims.text: EfOrderRepositoryTests is `(PostgresFixture database) : IClassFixture<PostgresFixture>, IAsyncLifetime`; its own InitializeAsync calls ResetAsync and runs before every test, since xUnit calls it on each new test class instance.
claims.source_hint: EfOrderRepositoryTests.cs:9-19; xunit.net docs: IAsyncLifetime on test classes

claims.text: No code in DonHang.Tests creates PostgresFixture for EfOrderRepositoryTests; xUnit creates it. PostgresFixture.InitializeAsync starts the container and applies migrations; DisposeAsync disposes the container.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: git grep 'new PostgresFixture' / PostgresFixture.cs:21-33

claims.text: xUnit calls a class fixture's DisposeAsync after the class's last test even when some tests in the class failed.
claims.source_hint: xunit.net docs: Shared Context (fixture cleanup after all tests in the class)

claims.text: One container per class instead of per test keeps the integration suite quick enough to run often.
`docker events --filter image=postgres:17.6-alpine --filter event=create` prints one line per container created from that image until stopped.

In a stage-2 checkout with Docker running, `dotnet test DonHang.Tests` passes 24 tests and docker events shows exactly two postgres:17.6-alpine creates; EfOrderRepositoryTests has 2 tests and OrdersApiTests 5.
